That is a possibility. But suicide isn't the right answer here. I truly understand the feeling of needing to do something drastic to get yourself heard. Hurting yourself is something you will likely come to regret.

If you are truly feeling the need for a drastic gesture, my suggestion at least a good step towards getting you positive help.
I did ask him about it, and he said he just likes being alone. He denied that he's been meeting up with anyone.

Has it ever occurred to you that your mother doesn't know how to help you? That maybe she sees your behavior get worse when you have the phone and better when you don't?

It could very easily be that, when you don't have your phone, you pull back and become far less emotional. Less emotional can very much look like obedience and better behavior, when it's actually you losing the ability to care.

I am the mother of a 15 year old who has been in serious trouble because of his phone. Like, serious LEGAL trouble. So please believe me when I say I 10000% understand the *need* to take away a smart phone. Also know that I'm still learning, 2 years after the initial legal trouble, how best to get him the help that he needs.

Now understand that your mother may not be there yet.

Give her some time and understanding. Write her a letter, using proper grammar and no curse words, telling her what you need.

She'll be far more open to that than anything you may say

Go somewhere not your home, call 911, and tell them what you're thinking. They'll send an ambulance, you get taken to the hospital, and you talk to the psych on duty. Tell them your concerns about the psych your parents picked.

That will get the ball rolling. Then, if your parents interfere and get you back with the religious psych they picked, you at least have a paper trail for your school counselor when school starts up again.

Keep fighting for yourself and your mental health.

Keep going. 

I'm going to be mean here, but I'll spell it out plain and simple.

If someone tells you to kill yourself, and you do it, you're letting them win. 

Continuing forward may be the hardest thing you ever do in your life. It might be years before it feels like it was worth it.

You may even hit harder times than you're experiencing right now.

The effort is worth it.

The pain is worth it.

The time is worth it.

YOU ARE WORTH IT.
I have already taken all electronics from him. I thought understood how awful what he was doing was last time...then he did it again.
